exercises.name: Modified side plank (on knee or with lower hip support)
Hip thrust with DB on hips
Step-ups onto a stable surface (low height)
incline DB push-up with lighter incline
Overhead press (neutral grip) with light DB
Split stance hip hinge (DB Romanian deadlift with staggered stance)
Farmer’s carry with light DBs (short distance)
Core breathing drill: diaphragmatic breathing with TVA activation
Bird-dog with hold at full extension
Core flow: 3 minutes continuous breathing with TVA cue
Push-ups with incline progression or full if ready
Core circuit: dead bug, side plank, bird-dog

notes: No jumping or high-impact moves in this block
Warm-up: 5–8 minutes locomotor work, hip hinge/shoulder prep, diaphragmatic breathing
Cool-down: 5–10 minutes gentle mobility and breathing
Core emphasis: TVA engagement, pelvic floor awareness
Breathing pattern: exhale on exertion, inhale during return
Progression principle: ease into loading, avoid full sit-ups/crunches
Pelvic floor: monitor leakage or heaviness; adjust intensity if symptoms occur
Each week includes 3 resistance sessions and 2 optional light mobility/rest days
Equipment: light dumbbells, resistance bands optional
Diastasis recti precautions: avoid any split-abs or Valsalva-heavy maneuvers
No crunches; anti-extension and anti-rotation core work favored
Optional progression after Week 4 to a 12-week plan can be tailored

raw_text:
Great—here’s a 4-week on-ramp block tailored for a client 10 weeks postpartum, cleared for moderate exercise with no jumping for the next 4 weeks. Home environment, light dumbbells, plus bodyweight. The goal is to re-establish movement quality, core engagement, form, and general conditioning, while respecting diastasis recti risk and pelvic floor health. Emphasize breath-driven core tasks, progressive loading, and recovery. Each week includes 3 resistance sessions and 2 optional, light mobility/rest days. Feel free to adjust based on her daily fluctuations.

Key postpartum considerations addressed
- Diastasis recti precautions: avoid any split-abs or Valsalva-heavy maneuvers; prioritize transverse abdominis engagement with hollowing cues and bracing with a neutral spine.
- Pelvic floor: monitor leakage, pelvic pressure, or heaviness; avoid heavy lifts or high-impact moves if sensation occurs.
- Breathing: nasal or diaphragmatic breathing with exhale during exertion cues; exhale on exertion and return to a controlled inhale.
- Progression principle: ease into loading, no crunches, avoid full sit-ups; favor anti-extension and anti-rotation core work.
- Recovery: daily light mobility, hydration, protein intake, and sleep optimization as feasible.

Program structure overview
- Frequency: 3 resistance sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Sat, for instance)
- Duration: ~30–45 minutes per session
- Equipment: Light dumbbells (adjust after Week 1 as tolerated), resistance bands optional
- Intensity: RPE 4–6/10 during main sets; ensure form quality over load
- Core emphasis: TVA engagement, pelvic floor awareness, dead bugs, bird-dogs, modified planks, side planks with regressions
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes locomotor work, hip hinge/shoulder prep, diaphragmatic breathing
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes gentle mobility and breathing

Week-by-week plan

Week 1: Acclimatisation and foundational mechanics
Goals: re-acclimate to exercise, re-establish breathing with core engagement, begin gentle strength with emphasis on form and pelvic floor.
Sessions: 3 (Day 1, Day 3, Day 5)

Session A (Full-body, emphasis on hips and spine)
- Warm-up (6–8 min): marching or step-touch, hip circles, cat-cow, diaphragmatic breathing 4-6 breaths per rep
- Goblet squat to chair (DB light): 2 sets x 12 reps (focus on depth to a comfortable position and bracing). Tempo: 2–0–2.
- Modified/Partial Romanian deadlift with DB: 2x12, hinge from hips, neutral spine, light weight.
- Push-up regression: incline push-ups on a bench or countertop: 2x10
- Bird-dog: 2x8 per side (focus on slow control, no trunk rotation)
- Side plank with knee down (or modified side plank on forearm and knee): 2x20–30 seconds per side
- Glute bridge (bodyweight or with light DB on hips): 2x12
- Cool-down: breathing flow and hip flexor stretch, 4–6 breaths per side

Session B (Upper body and core, minimal spine load)
- Warm-up: light cardio 4 minutes + scapular retractions, shoulder circles
- DB floor press (or incline floor press): 2x12
- Seated DB row (or standing with hinge): 2x12
- DB assisted shoulder lateral raise (light weight): 2x12
- Dead bug progression: 2x10 per side
- Modified side plank (on knee or with lower hip support): 2x20 seconds per side
- Pelvic floor engagement cue practice throughout: 3 sets of 10-second holds with 5-second rest
- Cool-down: gentle chest/lat stretch, thoracic mobility

Session C (Lower body emphasis + core stability)
- Warm-up: 5 minutes light cardio, hip hinge prep
- Chair squat: 3 sets x 12 (use chair for guidance)
- Hip thrust with DB on hips: 3x12
- Step-ups onto a stable surface (low height): 2x10 per leg
- Standing anti-rotation anti-rotation band-ish cue: 2x12 per side (rotation resisted via arms)
- Plank regressions: 3 x 15 seconds (on forearms/knees) if tolerable; otherwise hold a standing torso brace
- Cat-cow breathing sequence: 1–2 minutes
- Cool-down: hamstring/quad gentle release, glute stretch

Notes for Week 1
- Focus on form, diaphragmatic breathing with TVA engagement, and pelvic floor control.
- Do not push to failure; keep a calm, controlled tempo.
- If any diastasis discomfort or pelvic floor pressure arises, regress to more floor-based breathing drills and reduce loads.

Week 2: Progressive loading with increased volume
Goals: improve muscular endurance, reinforce core stability, begin light horizontal pulls and hip hinge patterns.
Sessions: 3 (Mon/Wed/Sat)

Session A
- Warm-up: 8 minutes total body mobility, breathing pattern
- Goblet squat: 3x12 (slightly deeper than Week 1, maintain form)
- DB Romanian deadlift: 3x12
- incline DB push-up with lighter incline: 3x10
- Dumbbell row (single-arm, supported): 3x12 per side
- Bird-dog: 3x10 per side
- Side plank (knee-down): 3x25 seconds per side
- Glute bridge march (one leg extended): 2x12 per leg
- Cool-down: hip flexor and chest stretch

Session B
- Warm-up: scapular prep, light band pull-aparts
- DB floor press: 3x12
- Seated row with DBs (or band): 3x12
- Overhead press (neutral grip) with light DB: 3x10
- Pallof press (anti-rotation) with light resistance: 3x10 per side
- Dead bug: 3x12 per side
- Plank: 3x20–25 seconds
- Cool-down: lat/shoulder/chest stretch

Session C
- Warm-up: 6–8 minutes dynamic
- Split stance hip hinge (DB Romanian deadlift with staggered stance): 3x12 per side
- Step-up to knee height: 3x12 per leg
- Glute bridge with march: 3x12
- DB glute/ham raise combo: 2x12
- Farmer’s carry with light DBs (short distance): 2x40–60 seconds
- Side plank (elbow): 3x30 seconds per side
- Core breathing drill: 2 minutes diaphragmatic breathing with TVA activation
- Cool-down: glute/hamstring stretch

Week 3: Introduce mild intensity and more control
Goals: enhance capacity while maintaining technique; slightly higher effort on core and anti-rotation.
Sessions: 3

Session A
- Warm-up: 8 minutes mobility + breathing
- Goblet squat with tempo: 3x10 (3 seconds down, 1 second up)
- DB Romanian deadlift: 3x12
- Push-up progression: incline to non-knee if tolerable: 3x8–10
- DB row with supported stance: 3x12
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- Bird-dog with hold at full extension: 3x8 per side
- Side plank with leg lift (if tolerates): 2x15 seconds per side
- Cool-down: hip flexor + thoracic mobility

Session B
- Warm-up: band pull-aparts, thoracic rotations
- DB floor press: 3x12
- Seated DB overhead press: 3x10
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift (light DB): 2x10 per leg
- Reverse lunge to row (lunge with DB row): 2x10 per leg
- Dead bug with extended limbs: 3x12 per side
- Plank with knee tuck (on knees or elevated): 3x12
- Cool-down: shoulder and hip mobility

Session C
- Warm-up: 6–8 minutes dynamic
- Hip thrust with DB: 3x12
- Step-ups with tempo: 3x12 per leg
- DB lateral raises: 3x12
- Farmer’s carry: 3x45–60 seconds
- Glute bridge variations (march or pulse): 2x15
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- Core flow: 3 minutes continuous breathing with TVA cue
- Cool-down: hamstring and hip flexor stretch

Week 4: Consolidation and tolerance toward a baseline
Goals: finalize ramp to baseline readiness; ensure consistency and readiness for a longer program. Sessions: 3

Session A
- Warm-up: 8 minutes mobility with breathing focus
- Goblet squat with moderate weight: 3x12
- DB Romanian deadlift: 3x12
- Push-ups with incline progression or full if ready: 3x10
- DB row: 3x12
- Pallof press or side press: 3x12 per side
- Bird-dog with brief hold: 3x10 per side
- Side plank: 3x30 seconds per side
- Optional 5-minute light cardio cool-down

Session B
- Warm-up: 6–8 minutes dynamic
- Step-ups with slight height increase: 3x12 per leg
- Hip thrust with DB: 3x12
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3x10
- DB curl to press: 2x12 (light)
- Dead bug with tempo: 3x12
- Farmer’s carry: 3x60 seconds
- Cool-down: full-body stretch and breathing

Session C
- Warm-up: 6–8 minutes mobility
- Split stance Romanian deadlift: 3x12 per leg
- DB bench press on floor: 3x12
- Lateral band steps (or DB carries if available): 2x15 steps
- Core circuit: 3 rounds of
  - Dead bug 12 per side
  - Side plank 25 seconds per side
  - Bird-dog 8 per side
- Cool-down: hip flexor and quad stretch

Optional progression guidelines
- If Week 4 feels too easy, add small increases: +2–3 reps per set, or add 1 extra set to main movements, or increase DB weight by small increments.
- If Week 4 feels too challenging at any time, regress to Week 2-3 loads and ensure form.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein: target 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and tissue repair. Spread across 3 main meals with a protein-rich snack post-workout.
- Hydration: ensure adequate fluids throughout the day; consider electrolytes if sweating heavily.
- Sleep and stress: prioritize consistent sleep windows; naps can aid recovery in the postpartum period.
- Fiber and gut health: include fiber-rich foods; monitor any constipation or digestion changes postpartum.
- Caffeine: limit if sensitive postpartum; if used, avoid close to bedtime.

Core and pelvic floor cues to use in every session
- TVA engagement cue: gently draw the lower belly in and up toward the spine as you exhale; maintain a neutral spine.
- Pelvic floor cue: gentle, slow, controlled contractions (like stopping the flow of urine) and full relax between reps; avoid breath-holding.
- Breathing pattern: inhale through nose to 4–6 seconds, exhale through mouth or nose to 4–6 seconds during exertion.

Notes for you as the trainer
- Monitor diastasis recti awareness. If she reports a doming along the midline during core work, regress to more foundational exercises (dead bug, bird-dog, clam shells with neutral spine, pelvic floor breathing) and reduce intra-abdominal pressure.
- No jumping or high-impact moves in this block. Do not introduce burpees or box jumps yet.
- Keep progressions conservative; postpartum recovery is highly individual. If fatigue, soreness, or pelvic floor symptoms appear, scale back one week and reassess.

Would you like me to tailor the plan to her current weight, current dumbbell weights, and preferred workout days, or add a simple 12-week progression after Week 4 that builds toward a more standard baseline (e.g., 3–4 days/week with progressive overload and a few conditioning days)?
